label: digit 0 input in the original phase (position >= 3)
explanation: Token detector for the digit 0 as an original-phase input at position t >= 3. 99.9% of activation mass is on in_tok == 0; never fires at t = 0..2, on the <DEL> step, or in the copy phase (even when 0 is fed back or output). Magnitude is highest for a first-occurrence 0 at mid positions (t = 4-6) preceded by letters (top examples ~2.4); it is weaker at t = 3 and for repeated 0s (in_first = 0 has 0.3x rate). False positives are mostly 0s at t = 3 or late 0s that stay silent; misses are tiny (<0.1% of mass) activations on other tokens.

issues: The core label and predicate hold up. On the test split, the predicate (in_tok==0)&(phase==0)&(t>=3) scores P 0.938, R 0.989, F1 0.963 and mass recall 0.999. Over all steps the feature never fires at t<3: '0 & phase0 & t<3' has P=0 over 50,529 steps. It never fires on 0s in the delimiter or copy phase either: '0 & phase!=0' has P=0 over 91,779 steps. The misses are scattered tiny activations on letters (for example x:0.07 or o:0.10) and hold 0.1% of the mass.

FALSE CLAIM: 'non-first occurrences fire at 0.3x the rate'. The 0.3x figure is the unconditional in_first lift over all steps, not a rate among 0 inputs. Among 0 inputs at t>=3 in the original phase, repeated 0s fire about as often as first ones: precision 0.914 for in_first==0 vs 0.942 for in_first==1. Mean activation per firing is only about 5% lower (mass_recall/recall 0.963 vs 1.017).

UNSUPPORTED CLAIM: 'strongest when it comes after letters'. Among predicate-true steps, a letter before the 0 and a digit before it give the same firing rate (P 0.937 vs 0.941). They also give the same mean magnitude (mass/recall about 1.01 in both cases). The top examples do favour g/j/y early in the sequence, but that is a token-identity effect, not a letters-vs-digits effect.
Magnitude claims partly check out. Mass per firing is lowest at t=3, where 0s hold 24% of the active steps but only 10.7% of the mass. It peaks around t=5-6, which is roughly consistent with 't=4-6'.

False positives are concentrated, as the explanation says. About 3,270 are 0s at t=3 (precision 0.80 there, vs at least 0.99 at t=4..7) and about 290 are 0s at t=8 (precision 0.90). I tested the t=3 silences against L, the previous token's class, earlier digits, digits at positions 0-1, and first vs repeated 0, and none of these separates them; precision stays near 0.80 throughout. They look like weak activations at t=3 falling below the activation threshold, not a clean subclass. Excluding t=3 lowers F1 to 0.855, so the original predicate remains the best one I found.

Verdict: the label and predicate are right, but the explanation contains one false quantitative claim (the 0.3x rate for repeated 0s) and one unsupported one (stronger after letters). It should be corrected before recording.
